chunk_findings.detail:
`total` is captured before `f.limit` truncates `rows`, but `live` is computed *after* the truncation:

```python
total = len(rows)
if f.limit:
    rows = rows[: f.limit]
...
live = sum(1 for r in rows if r["status"] == "accepted")
```

So `live` counts only the retained page while `total` counts the whole filtered set, and the two no longer describe the same population. Concrete input: 10 decisions all with status `accepted`, called with `--limit 3`. The function returns `total=10`, `shown=3`, `live=3`, so any header/template rendering "{{live}} live of {{total}}" reports "3 live of 10" even though there are 10 accepted decisions and nothing was superseded. The sibling keys `total`/`shown` are both population-consistent (`total` for the filtered set, `shown` for the page); `live` is the only one silently measured on the truncated page, which contradicts its name. Computing `live` before applying `f.limit` (as an overall statistic) is what the rest of the return shape implies.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_decisions.py:44 (the `live` computation in `data`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`_touched` guards the end of the window (`hi = s.ended_at or "9999"`) but uses `s.started_at` raw for the low bound. `data()` itself, twelve lines later, writes `opened = s.started_at or (s.prompts[0]["at"] if s.prompts else "")` — i.e. the same module acknowledges that `started_at` can be falsy. When it is:

- If `started_at` is `None`, `ts >= lo` on line with `if ts >= lo and ts <= hi` raises `TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'NoneType'`. `_touched(q)` is called unconditionally before the session loop, so a single such session aborts the whole SESSION export with a traceback rather than degrading.
- If `started_at` is `""`, `ts >= ""` is true for every timestamp string, so the lower bound disappears and the window becomes `(-inf, s.ended_at]`: every `item.started`/`lease.acquired`/`item.completed`/`worktree.merged` event that agent ever emitted before the session ended — including items from *previous* sessions — is attributed as "touched" by this session. Given fixture data where one agent works across many sessions, `items_text` for each session then lists other sessions' items.

Note that `data()`'s `since` filter does not mask this, because `_touched` is computed for every session regardless of `f.since`/`f.session`. The fix is to use the same fallback (`lo = s.started_at or <first prompt at> or "0000"`) that `data()` already uses for `opened`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_sessions.py `_touched` (`lo = s.started_at`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_limit` is documented as "Keep the newest `n` lines (days are newest first)", but the lines *inside* a day are built oldest-first: `rows = sorted(days[day], key=lambda g: g["sort"])` sorts ascending on `(ts, subject)`. Slicing `d["lines"][:left]` therefore keeps the **oldest** lines of each day, not the newest. Concrete failure: day `2024-05-02` has lines at `10:00`, `11:00`, `12:00`; day `2024-05-01` (older) has a `15:00` line. With `limit=2` the newest two lines in the log are `11:00` and `12:00` of `2024-05-02`, but the code returns `10:00` and `11:00` of `2024-05-02`, silently dropping the `12:00` entry. Within a partially-taken newest day the slice must come from the end (`d["lines"][-left:]`), otherwise `--limit` yields the wrong entries.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_worklog.py:200 (`_limit`, `take = d["lines"][:left]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The session template renders every field named in the export spec except the session handoff. `sessions.md.j2` lines 5–31 iterate `s.prompts`, `s.notes` and `s.imported_notes` and print `s.items_text`, but there is no `{{ s.handoff }}` (or equivalent) anywhere in the loop body. Concretely, for any session whose data carries a handoff blob — the case the intent explicitly calls out with "…items touched, handoff" — the generated `sessions.md` silently drops it, so the exported session document is missing the one field that is supposed to let a later reader resume the work. Since this is the only session template in the change, the field is never exported at all, not merely relocated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/sessions.md.j2

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture for `T-fix` stamps its three coalesced events in the order `worktree.merged` = 2026-09-20T15:00:00Z, `item.completed` = 2026-09-20T15:01:00Z, `bug.fixed` = 2026-09-20T15:02:00Z, and the fixture comment right above them describes the line as "merged, completed and its bug fixed" (the intent likewise says the log is chronological / "its merge, completion and bug-fixed events coalesced"). The assertion, however, requires the literal status string `**completed, merged, bug fixed**`, i.e. completion *before* merge. Given exactly this input, any implementation that renders the coalesced status label in the order the events occurred (or in the order named by the intent) produces `merged, completed, bug fixed`, so `lines[0]` does not contain the asserted substring and the acceptance test fails; conversely, the only way the assertion passes is for the export to deliberately order completion ahead of a merge that happened a minute earlier, which contradicts the fixture's own timestamps/comment and the stated "chronological" requirement. Either the fixture timestamps (merged should be after completed, e.g. 15:01/15:02) or the asserted string (should be `merged, completed, bug fixed`) is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_docs_b.py::test_worklog_coalesces_one_item_into_one_line

chunk_findings.detail: `_touched` sets `lo = s.started_at` and then compares `ts >= lo` inside the per-agent loop, but `data` (line 78: `opened = s.started_at or (s.prompts[0]["at"] if s.prompts else "")`) and the `hi = s.ended_at or "9999"` line right below both treat the session timestamps as possibly absent/None. If a session has no `started_at` (the very case `data` guards against) *and* its `s.agent` has any event in `_WORK` (`item.started`/`lease.acquired`/`item.completed`/`worktree.merged`), the loop body executes and evaluates `ts >= None`, raising `TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'NoneType'`. The guard that makes this reachable is exactly the one `data` already contains, so the two call sites disagree about whether `started_at` can be missing: `data` tolerates it, `_touched` crashes. Given such a session (agent named, no `started_at`, with a work event in the window), `data` never returns — the whole SESSION export fails instead of falling back to the first prompt's timestamp as the caller expects.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_sessions.py:56 (`_touched`, `lo = s.started_at`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_limit` claims to "keep the newest ``n`` lines (days are newest first)", but within a day the lines were sorted ascending by time (`rows = sorted(days[day], key=lambda g: g["sort"])`, where `g["sort"]` is the *earliest* ts via `min(...)`), i.e. oldest line first. So `take = d["lines"][:left]` slices off the *oldest* lines of the newest day and discards the newest ones. Concrete failure: one day with lines at 09:00, 12:00 and 17:00 and `--limit 1` returns the 09:00 line (and `entries: 1`), even though the newest line asked for is the 17:00 one. If the day spans the limit, the output silently omits the most recent events; only when the limit crosses a whole day does the day-level "newest first" ordering save it. To keep the newest `n` it must take from the end of each day's (ascending) list, or the per-day list must be emitted newest-first consistently with `_limit`'s assumption.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_worklog.py:_limit (and the sort in `data`)

chunk_findings.detail: The row template emits decision metadata without escaping pipe characters (or newlines) that are legal in a decision title or in the `governs` value. A title such as `Support A | B selector` is written to the "Title" cell verbatim, so the emitted row has one more `|` than the header/separator rows have columns. Given a decision with that title the table renders with the trailing columns shifted (and a newline in a title truncates the row entirely), so the "Date"/"Title"/"Governs" cells no longer line up with the header — the index is misrendered for a perfectly valid input. The fix is to escape `|` (and collapse newlines) per cell, e.g. `{{ r.title | replace('|', '\\|') }}`, or build the cells with a table-aware escape. The same applies to `r.governs`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/decisions.md.j2:8

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "**completed, merged, bug fixed**" in lines[0]` expects the coalesced T-fix line to list the completion before the merge. But the fixture emits the events in chronological order: `worktree.merged` at 15:00, `item.completed` at 15:01, then `bug.fixed` at 15:02, and the intent explicitly requires the worklog to be chronological. A correct chronological coalescing therefore renders “**merged, completed, bug fixed**”, not “**completed, merged, bug fixed**”. The test’s own comment (“merged, completed and its bug fixed”) confirms the intended order, so the expected string is internally inconsistent with the fixture and will fail against a correct implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_docs_b.py::test_worklog_coalesces_one_item_into_one_line

chunk_findings.detail: `_opened()` returns the empty string for a session that has neither `started_at` nor prompts ("else unknown"), and `_touched` feeds that straight into the window predicate `if ts >= lo and ts <= hi`. In Python any timestamp string satisfies `ts >= ""`, so for such a session the predicate degenerates to `ts <= hi` and *every* work event belonging to that agent (`by_agent.get(s.agent, ())` = `item.started`/`lease.acquired`/`item.completed`/`worktree.merged` across the whole log) is attributed to that session. Given input such as an imported/journal session with `agent="alice"`, `started_at=None`, `prompts=[]`, `notes=[]`, and an agent history of "alice" touching items A–Z over many months, `_touched` returns `{that_session: {A…Z}}`, so the SESSION export's "items touched" lists the agent's entire history for a session that touched nothing — and every other session of the same agent gets the same over-broad set if it too lacks a start. The previous code (`lo = s.started_at` → `None`) raised `TypeError: '>=' not supported between 'str' and 'NoneType'` instead of silently emitting wrong data, so this change replaces a loud failure with incorrect output; an unbounded lower bound needs an explicit sentinel (e.g. `"0000"`) or a guard, not `""`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_sessions.py:57 (`lo = _opened(s)` in `_touched`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `take = d["lines"][-left:]` produces a non-contiguous selection whenever `days` is iterated oldest-first (its insertion order, since `days` is a plain dict filled via `setdefault` while processing and the `for d in days:` loop is unchanged and adds no reverse). `left` starts at the cap and is consumed from the *oldest* day forward, taking each day's *tail*. Concrete case: cap = 10, oldest day has 3 lines, next day has 20 lines. Iteration 1 takes all 3 of the oldest day (`[-10:]` clamps), `left` becomes 7; iteration 2 takes the last 7 of the second day, `left` becomes 0. The export therefore emits the entire oldest day plus only the *tail* of the second day, silently skipping the middle 13 lines of that day and dropping every later day — a gap that is neither the earliest nor the latest N lines, which is plainly wrong for a bounded/limited worklog. The old `[:left]` at least produced a contiguous prefix. The added comment ("lines inside a day run oldest to newest") only justifies the per-day direction; it does not fix the fact that consuming the budget from the oldest day's tail creates a hole in the middle of the kept range (to keep the most recent lines, the day loop would have to iterate newest-first, e.g. `reversed(days)`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_worklog.py:203

chunk_findings.detail: The truncation side was flipped from `d["lines"][:left]` to `d["lines"][-left:]`, but the day iteration order and the emitted `kept` order were not touched, and the export is specified as chronological (oldest day first). Within a day the lines run oldest→newest, so `[-left:]` takes the *newest* lines of a day while the loop still walks days from oldest to newest, producing a non-contiguous, wrong selection whenever the window exceeds the cap. Concrete case: `days = [day1(oldest, A1,A2,A3), day2(newer, B1,B2,B3)]` and `left = 4`. First iteration takes `day1.lines[-4:]` = `A1,A2,A3` (all three), leaving `left = 1`; second iteration takes `day2.lines[-1:]` = `B3`. Result `A1,A2,A3,B3` keeps the *earliest* lines of the oldest day (`A1`, older than anything in `day2`) while silently dropping the newer `B1,B2`. That is neither the first four lines (`A1,A2,A3,B1`, what `[:left]` gave and what an oldest-first chronological listing truncated to a prefix should be) nor the most recent four (`A3,B1,B2,B3`). To keep the tail of the window the day iteration would have to be reversed as well; with the current ordering `[:left]` was the coherent choice, so this change is wrong for any input whose worklog window contains more lines than the cap.
